This vignette explains how to use `gfw_vessel_insights()` to retrieve vessel-level
indicators from the Global Fishing Watch (GFW) Insights API. It shows how to get
the `vesselId`s that the function needs, what the response contains, how to turn
it into a table with one row per vessel, and how to move from a count in the
insights to the events behind it with `gfw_event()`.

> **Note:**
> Insights are meant to support risk-based decision-making. They are indicators,
not conclusions. See the
[Insights API documentation](https://globalfishingwatch.org/our-apis/documentation#insights-api),
and the [Terms of Use](https://globalfishingwatch.org/our-apis/documentation#terms-of-use)
in the [GFW API documentation](https://globalfishingwatch.org/our-apis/documentation#introduction)
before drawing conclusions from them.

You need a GFW API access token stored in the `GFW_TOKEN` environment variable
(see the [Authorization section of the README](https://github.com/GlobalFishingWatch/gfwr#authorization)
to request and save a token).
`gfw_auth()` reads it for you.


## What are vessel insights?

The Insights API combines information on a vessel's observed activity (mostly
derived from AIS), vessel identity records, and public authorizations into a set
of indicators. The idea is to help you decide which vessels deserve a closer
look, for example for due diligence or for planning an inspection.

With `gfw_vessel_insights()` you choose which indicators to request with the
`includes` argument:

| `includes` value | Question it helps answer |
|:-------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------|
| `"FISHING"` | Did the vessel have apparent fishing events inside no-take MPAs, or in areas with no known RFMO authorization? |
| `"GAP"` | Did the vessel have AIS disabling events ("gaps")? |
| `"COVERAGE"` | How well was the vessel tracked by AIS receivers? |
| `"VESSEL-IDENTITY-IUU-VESSEL-LIST"` | Is the vessel present on an RFMO IUU vessel list? |
| `"VESSEL-IDENTITY-FLAG-CHANGES"` | Did the vessel change flag? (see [Access to some insights](#access-to-some-insights)) |
| `"VESSEL-IDENTITY-MOU-LIST"` | Is the vessel's flag state on a Tokyo or Paris MOU black or grey list? (see [Access to some insights](#access-to-some-insights)) |

You also have to give a period (`start_date` and `end_date`, as `"YYYY-MM-DD"`
or `Date`) and one or more `vessels`, a character vector of `vesselId`s.


## Step 1: get the `vesselId`

`gfw_vessel_insights()` works with `vesselId`s, not with MMSI or ship names. If
you only know an MMSI, an IMO number or a ship name, find the `vesselId` first
with `gfw_vessel_info()`. See the
[identity vignette](https://globalfishingwatch.github.io/gfwr/articles/identity.html)
for details on what a `vesselId` is and why one vessel can have several.

In this vignette we use three `vesselId`s that are also used in the examples of
the function documentation. We use `gfw_vessel_info()` to see which vessels they
correspond to:

```{r vessel_ids}
vessel_ids <- c(
  "785101812-2127-e5d2-e8bf-7152c5259f5f",
  "2339c52c3-3a84-1603-f968-d8890f23e1ed",
  "2d26aa452-2d4f-4cae-2ec4-377f85e88dcb"
)

vessel_names <- map(
  vessel_ids,
  \(id) {
    gfw_vessel_info(ids = id, search_type = "id", quiet = TRUE)$selfReportedInfo |>
      filter(vesselId == id) |>
      select(vesselId, shipname, flag, ssvid) |>
      distinct()
  }
) |>
  list_rbind()

vessel_names
```


## Step 2: request insights for one vessel

We ask for four insights for the first vessel over a period of five years.

```{r one_vessel}
insights <- gfw_vessel_insights(
  includes = c("COVERAGE", "FISHING", "GAP", "VESSEL-IDENTITY-IUU-VESSEL-LIST"),
  start_date = "2020-01-01",
  end_date = "2025-03-03",
  vessels = vessel_ids[1]
)

insights
```

The result is a one-row tibble. Each column is an insight, and each column is a
**list-column**, so the content of each insight sits inside the cell. The
columns are:

- `period`: the dates you requested.
- `vesselIdsWithoutIdentity`: meant for `vesselId`s without an identity record.
It was empty in all our examples, including a request with an ID that does not
exist, so do not rely on it to detect wrong IDs (see
[Common errors](#common-errors)).
- `coverage`, `gap`, `apparentFishing` and `vesselIdentity`: one column per
insight type requested.

To open an insight, take the first element of the list-column:

```{r open_gap}
insights$gap[[1]]$periodSelectedCounters
```

`periodSelectedCounters` gives counts for the period you requested. Here
`eventsGapOff` is the number of AIS disabling events in that period.

The other insights follow the same pattern:

```{r open_others}
# Counts of apparent fishing events, including events in no-take MPAs and in
# areas with no known RFMO authorization
insights$apparentFishing[[1]]$periodSelectedCounters

# AIS coverage
insights$coverage[[1]]

# Presence on an RFMO IUU vessel list
insights$vesselIdentity[[1]]$iuuVesselList
```

__How to read each one__

- __`apparentFishing`__ gives the number of *apparent* fishing events. They are
model-based detections, not confirmed fishing. `eventsInNoTakeMPAs` and `eventsInRFMOWithoutKnownAuthorization`
are the subset that fall inside no-take MPAs or in RFMO areas where GFW has no
record of an authorization for the vessel. A missing authorization can also mean
that the authorization data is incomplete, so treat it as a reason to look
further and not as proof of a violation.
- __`gap`__ counts AIS disabling events. A gap can have many causes, including
poor satellite reception and equipment problems, and it does not by itself mean
that a vessel was hiding its activity.
- __`coverage`__ is the AIS coverage metric for the vessel. It is reported as a
`percentage`, together with the counts of `blocks` and `blocksWithPositions` it
is based on. Check the Insights API documentation for how it is defined before
you use it to compare vessels.
- __`iuuVesselList`__ reports how many times the vessel has been listed
(`totalTimesListed`) and how many of those fall inside your period
(`totalTimesListedInThePeriod`).

The datasets used for each insight are shown in the `datasets` element of each
list, which is useful to cite and to detect changes in dataset versions.


## One row per vessel, or one combined result?

You can pass several `vesselId`s to `vessels`, but be careful: __the API returns
one combined result for all the vessels you send, not one result per vessel__.

We can check this by running the same request for each vessel separately and
summing the counts:

```{r per_vessel}
requested_insights <- c("COVERAGE", "FISHING", "GAP", "VESSEL-IDENTITY-IUU-VESSEL-LIST")

summarise_insights <- function(vessel_id) {
  x <- gfw_vessel_insights(
    includes = requested_insights,
    start_date = "2020-01-01",
    end_date = "2025-03-03",
    vessels = vessel_id
  )

  tibble(
    vesselId = vessel_id,
    coverage_pct = x$coverage[[1]]$percentage,
    fishing_events = x$apparentFishing[[1]]$periodSelectedCounters$events,
    fishing_in_no_take_mpas = x$apparentFishing[[1]]$periodSelectedCounters$eventsInNoTakeMPAs,
    fishing_without_rfmo_auth = x$apparentFishing[[1]]$periodSelectedCounters$eventsInRFMOWithoutKnownAuthorization,
    ais_off_events = x$gap[[1]]$periodSelectedCounters$eventsGapOff,
    iuu_listings = x$vesselIdentity[[1]]$iuuVesselList$totalTimesListed
  )
}

per_vessel <- map(vessel_ids, summarise_insights) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  left_join(vessel_names, by = "vesselId") |>
  relocate(shipname, flag, .after = vesselId) |>
  select(-ssvid, -vesselId)

per_vessel
```

Now the same request with the three `vesselId`s together:

```{r combined}
combined <- gfw_vessel_insights(
  includes = requested_insights,
  start_date = "2020-01-01",
  end_date = "2025-03-03",
  vessels = vessel_ids
)

combined$apparentFishing[[1]]$periodSelectedCounters$events
combined$gap[[1]]$periodSelectedCounters$eventsGapOff

# Compare with the sum of the individual requests
sum(per_vessel$fishing_events)
sum(per_vessel$ais_off_events)
```

The counts of the combined request match the sums of the individual requests.
Percentages such as `coverage` are not summed: the combined value is a single
figure for the request, not the sum of the individual ones.

This gives you two ways of working, depending on your question:

- To __compare vessels__, send one request per vessel, as in `summarise_insights()`
above, and bind the results into a table.
- To __summarise a vessel that has several `vesselId`s__ over time (see the
[identity vignette](https://globalfishingwatch.github.io/gfwr/articles/identity.html)),
send all its `vesselId`s in one request to get a single combined result.

> **Note:**
> Each request counts against your API rate limits. When you loop over many
vessels, avoid running the loop repeatedly. See the
[GFW API documentation](https://globalfishingwatch.org/our-apis/documentation#introduction)
for the current limits.


## From counts to events

The insights give you counts and lists of event identifiers, not the details of
each event. To find out when and where something happened, use `gfw_event()`
with the same vessel and period. For example, the first vessel has
`r per_vessel$ais_off_events[1]` AIS disabling events in the period:

```{r gap_events}
gaps <- gfw_event(
  event_type = "GAP",
  vessels = vessel_ids[1],
  start_date = "2020-01-01",
  end_date = "2025-03-03",
  quiet = TRUE
)

gaps |>
  select(eventId, start, end, lat, lon)
```

The number of rows matches `eventsGapOff` in the insights. The other event types
available in `gfw_event()` (fishing, port visits, encounters and loitering) are
described in the [events vignette](https://globalfishingwatch.github.io/gfwr/articles/fishing_activity_maps.html).


## Access to some insights

The `"VESSEL-IDENTITY-FLAG-CHANGES"` and `"VESSEL-IDENTITY-MOU-LIST"` insights are
accepted by `gfw_vessel_insights()`, but they may not be available to all users.
With a standard API token the API can answer with a `403 Forbidden` error stating
that you do not have permission to request those insights. If this happens, remove
them from `includes` and request the other insights. If you need them, contact
the GFW API team.

```{r forbidden, eval = FALSE}
gfw_vessel_insights(
  includes = c("VESSEL-IDENTITY-FLAG-CHANGES", "VESSEL-IDENTITY-MOU-LIST"),
  start_date = "2020-01-01",
  end_date = "2025-03-03",
  vessels = vessel_ids[1]
)
```


## Common errors

`gfw_vessel_insights()` checks your input before it contacts the API, so most
mistakes return a clear message:

```{r errors, error = TRUE}
# An insight type that does not exist
gfw_vessel_insights(
  includes = "FOO",
  start_date = "2020-01-01",
  end_date = "2025-03-03",
  vessels = vessel_ids[1]
)

# Start date after end date
gfw_vessel_insights(
  includes = "GAP",
  start_date = "2025-03-03",
  end_date = "2020-01-01",
  vessels = vessel_ids[1]
)
```

__Check your `vesselId`s__. The function only checks that `vessels` is a
non-empty character vector, not that the IDs exist. With some combinations of
insights, an ID that does not exist returns empty results and zero counts, with
no error, which looks the same as a vessel with nothing to report. With other
combinations (for example when `"COVERAGE"` is requested) the API returns an
error. Always get your `vesselId`s from `gfw_vessel_info()` and treat a vessel
with all zeros and no coverage with suspicion until you have checked its ID.

If you contact the GFW team about a problem, use `print_request = TRUE` and send
the printed request.
